questions.q: Which three components replace the combustion engine, gearbox and clutch in an electric vehicle?
options: A traction battery, an electric motor and an inverter
A small battery, a generator and an electric clutch
An electric motor, a gearbox and an electric clutch
A 12V battery, a starter motor and a catalytic converter
questions.explain: An electric vehicle is driven by a traction battery, an electric motor and an inverter that converts between direct and alternating current.

questions.q: Why is a single fixed gear enough in most electric vehicles, without a multi-speed gearbox?
options: Because the electric motor gives almost all of its torque from a standstill, across a wide range of speeds
Because an electric motor can't spin fast enough to need an extra gear
Because their maximum speed is limited by law
Because the law bans gearboxes in electric vehicles
questions.explain: Unlike a combustion engine, an electric motor gives high torque almost from the first moment and keeps it across a wide range — so a single gear is enough for most vehicles.

questions.q: What is the role of the inverter in an electric vehicle?
options: To convert between the battery's direct current and the motor's alternating current, and back again
To raise the voltage of the 12V battery
To filter air pollution from the vehicle's exhaust
To slow the motor's revolutions before they reach the wheels
questions.explain: The battery works in direct current (DC) and the electric motor in alternating current (AC); the inverter converts between them in both directions.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a full hybrid and a mild hybrid?
options: A mild hybrid is faster on the expressway
Only the mild hybrid can be charged from a power outlet
There's no practical difference between the two
A full hybrid can drive the vehicle on electric power alone for short distances; a mild hybrid only assists the combustion engine
questions.explain: In a mild hybrid, the electric motor only assists and doesn't drive the vehicle alone; in a full hybrid it can drive the vehicle by itself for short distances at low speed.

questions.q: How is the battery charged in a regular hybrid that isn't a plug-in hybrid?
options: Only from a fast public charging station
It has no chargeable battery
Only from a home power outlet
Only from the engine and regenerative braking — it can't be plugged into electricity
questions.explain: A hybrid that isn't a plug-in generates its own electricity from the engine and from regenerative braking; only a plug-in hybrid also connects to a charging station.

questions.q: In which type of driving does a hybrid save the most fuel compared with an ordinary vehicle?
options: Towing a caravan up a long climb
There's no difference between types of driving
Slow urban driving with lots of stopping and slowing down
Fast, steady driving on the expressway
questions.explain: In urban driving with lots of stops, the hybrid recycles braking energy that would be lost in an ordinary vehicle; on a fast, steady expressway the advantage is much smaller.

questions.q: What is the main difference between AC charging and fast DC charging?
options: There's no difference in speed, only in price
AC is only for trucks, DC for private cars
Fast DC charging feeds direct current straight into the battery and is much faster than AC
DC is only available at home, AC only on non-urban roads
questions.explain: AC charging passes through the vehicle's onboard charger and is relatively slow; fast DC charging feeds direct current straight into the battery and charges a large part of it in under half an hour.

questions.q: Which charging connectors are common in Israel?
options: Type 2 for AC charging, CCS for fast DC charging
USB-C only, for all types of charging
Type 1 for fast charging, CCS for regular charging
Only a regular household plug, with no dedicated connector
questions.explain: In Israel the common connector for AC charging is Type 2, and for fast DC charging it's CCS, which adds two large pins to the connector.

questions.q: Why does the rate of fast DC charging drop gradually as the battery approaches a full charge?
options: So as not to overheat the battery
To save the company money on electricity
The law requires slowing down above 50% charge
It's a common fault at charging stations
questions.explain: Fast charging generates heat; as the battery approaches full, the station slows the charging rate to protect it from overheating.

questions.q: What is correct behaviour at a public charging station?
options: To park in a charging bay without charging, if there's space
To leave the cable stretched across the pavement until you return
To leave the vehicle parked at the station even after charging has finished, as a reserve
To free up the station once charging has finished, so the next vehicle can charge
questions.explain: Public charging stations are a shared resource — you should move the vehicle as soon as charging finishes and not block it unnecessarily.

questions.q: Why does a driver new to an electric vehicle need an especially light touch on the accelerator?
options: Because the electric motor gives maximum torque almost from the first moment, and it's easy to accelerate more than planned
Because the law requires gentle acceleration in an electric vehicle
Because the accelerator pedal in an electric vehicle is slower to respond
Because the pedal is more prone to faults
questions.explain: The instant response of the electric motor can surprise drivers used to a combustion engine, causing sharper acceleration than planned.

questions.q: What does regenerative braking do in an electric vehicle?
options: Slows the vehicle using the motor as a generator, while charging the battery at the same time
Disconnects the regular brakes completely
Only works at high speed above 100 km/h
Completely replaces the need for emergency braking
questions.explain: When you lift your foot off the accelerator, the electric motor turns into a generator, slowing the vehicle and charging the battery. It doesn't replace emergency braking with the brake pedal.

questions.q: Which of the following factors shortens an electric vehicle's actual range the most?
options: Fast driving with sharp acceleration and braking, and cold weather
The size of the boot
The colour of the vehicle
An engine oil change
questions.explain: High speed, cold (which reduces battery efficiency), load and aggressive driving significantly shorten the actual range compared with the figure in the brochure.

questions.q: Why do you need special attention to pedestrians when driving an electric vehicle at low speed?
options: Because the vehicle is too brightly lit
Because the Traffic Ordinance bans electric vehicles from driving near pedestrians
Because the vehicle is almost silent at low speed, and it's hard to hear it approaching
Because an electric vehicle always drives faster near pedestrian crossings
questions.explain: Without the noise of a combustion engine, an electric vehicle at low speed is hard to hear — so you need double the attention near pedestrian crossings and car parks.

questions.q: What is the first and most important rule about orange cables on an electric or hybrid vehicle?
options: Never touch or cut them — they may only be handled by a qualified vehicle electrician
You may touch them only with household rubber gloves
You may touch them when the vehicle is switched off
They are only for decoration and carry no voltage
questions.explain: Orange cables belong to the high-voltage system, which can be fatal on direct contact. They may only be handled by a vehicle electrician who has had dedicated training.

questions.q: What do you do if you see smoke or a leaking fluid from the floor of an electric vehicle that has been in a crash?
options: Keep driving to get away from the dangerous area
Pour water on the area immediately
Move away and call the Fire and Rescue Services, stating that it's an electric vehicle
Open the bonnet to check the source of the problem
questions.explain: A traction battery fire is different from a fuel fire and needs professional firefighting. Move away, call the Fire and Rescue Services {{fact:emergency.fire_and_rescue}} and state that it's an electric or hybrid vehicle.

questions.q: An electric vehicle has been fully flooded, with water above floor level. What is the correct thing to do?
options: Wait for the water to recede and drive as usual
Try to start the vehicle immediately to get it out of the water
Disconnect the 12V battery — that's enough to drive safely
Tow the vehicle and have the high-voltage system checked at an authorised garage before trying to start it
questions.explain: Full flooding can damage the high-voltage system. The vehicle is towed and checked at an authorised garage before anyone tries to start it again.

questions.q: Why must many electric vehicles not be towed with the driven wheels touching the road, without checking the manufacturer's instructions?
options: Because it only reduces driving range, with no damage
Because the law bans towing any electric vehicle in any situation
Because it's only banned for new private vehicles
Because the driven wheels turning can activate the electric motor as a generator and damage the system
questions.explain: When towed with driven wheels on the road, the wheels turning can activate the motor as a generator and cause damage — so tow according to the manufacturer's instructions, usually with all four wheels lifted.

questions.q: Why is it important to bring an electric vehicle for a periodic brake check, even if the pads are still thick?
options: Because regenerative braking damages the brake pads
Because a brake that is barely used (thanks to regenerative braking) can rust and stick
Because the brakes in an electric vehicle wear out faster than in an ordinary vehicle
Because the law requires a monthly brake check only for electric vehicles
questions.explain: Regenerative braking greatly reduces the use of the regular brakes, so they can rust and stick without regular use — which is why a periodic check is still needed.

questions.q: Why won't an electric vehicle with a flat 12V battery “wake up”, even if its traction battery is full?
options: Because an electric vehicle has no electrical operating system
Because an electric vehicle has no 12V battery at all
Because the traction battery depends entirely on the 12V battery in order to charge
Because the 12V battery powers the computers and systems that operate the vehicle, separately from the traction battery
questions.explain: The regular 12V battery still exists in an electric vehicle and powers the operating systems, lighting and computers — without it the vehicle won't wake up even if the traction battery is full.
